subject: Urgent: Unusual API activity — forensic handoff & SIG/CAIQ evidence request
messages:
From: Jessica Park <jessica@aurelius-labs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@aurelius-labs.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual API traffic observed — immediate assistance requested

Hi Mateo,

We detected sustained, anomalous usage of our integration with Redwood between 01:30–02:40 UTC this morning: requests from an API key tied to our staging org that performed large-scale embeddings and a few long-completion calls. We throttled the key and rotated secrets, but we need Redwood to help with:

- A timeline of the inbound requests (IP, user-agent, timestamps) seen on your side for org ID aurel-ct-9
- Any offered indicators of compromise: unusual worker IDs, model variant fallbacks, or cross-customer routing artifacts
- Recommended containment steps and the Redwood IRP contact for postmortem

We are preparing a customer notification and will likely need SOC 2 / SIG artifacts for our security team (evidence that access was isolated, redaction steps, and log exports).

Please escalate to your security & compliance team and advise next steps. We would like a short conference call today if possible.

Thanks,
Jessica Park
Security Operations
Aurelius Labs
[Attachment: example_request_sample.json (snippet)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@aurelius-labs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API traffic observed — immediate assistance requested

Thanks Jessica — sending to our incident triage team now and marking this high priority. Short answers up front:

1) We will gather a time-ordered request export for the window you listed and provide IPs, user-agent strings, and request hashes.
2) We'll check for cross-tenant routing indicators and any abnormal kernel fallbacks in the serving logs.
3) Our on-call IR lead is Marissa Cole (security lead); Karhtik will pull infra traces.

Action items we will take by EOD:
- Forensic telemetry export (redis/kvcache call traces, LB logs) for 01:00–03:00 UTC [will provide secure link]
- Short containment summary and recommended steps (rotated keys are good; we'll confirm no read escalation)
- SIG/SOC 2 evidence subset: access logs, role change audit, and retention-policy snapshot

Marissa / Karthik / Neha — can you confirm ownership for the artifacts below and an ETA? Also please advise whether we should suspend any regional routing for Aurelius while we investigate.

—Mateo
Product Security, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 415 555 0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica@aurelius-labs.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API traffic observed — forensic artifacts attached and SIG/CAIQ ask

Hi Jessica — Marissa from IR/forensics here. We prioritized a telemetry snapshot and basic containment summary. Please find the initial package attached and a short index below.

Attachments (stubs):
- telemetry_extract_aurelius_20260807.tar.gz (45MB, tar.gz) — time-ordered request logs, edge LB logs, and service request hashes.
- auth_trace_20260807.csv (2MB, csv) — token usage, session IDs, and rotated-key timestamps.
- redwood_irp_v2.pdf (1.2MB, pdf) — current incident response playbook excerpt (preserve/immediate steps).

Index (high level):
- 01:26–01:33 UTC: repeated long-completion calls from two IPs (see lb_edges/ips.csv).
- 01:34 UTC: automatic rate-limiter triggered and one token flagged for throttling; we observed fallback to a smaller model variant for several requests — no evidence of cross-tenant data leaks in the sampled KV cache.
- 01:40–02:00 UTC: additional requests from rotating IPs; we are collecting full request-body samples where allowed by retention rules.

Open items / asks for Aurelius:
- If you have sample request bodies (we received a snippet), please share the full sample for correlation.
- Confirm whether any data-access requests were made from internal Aurelius user accounts during the window.
- We will prepare a SIG/CAIQ crosswalk excerpt focused on the control families relevant to this event (access control and logging) — ETA: Monday 2026-08-10.

Proposed next step: 30-minute bridge today at 16:00 UTC to go over the artifacts and agree on redaction/packaging for SOC 2 reporting. Is that workable?

[Quoted below — Jessica's original message]
> We detected sustained, anomalous usage of our integration with Redwood between 01:30–02:40 UTC this morning: requests from an API key tied to our staging org that performed large-scale embeddings and a few long-completion calls. We throttled the key and rotated secrets, but we need Redwood to help with:
>
> - A timeline of the inbound requests (IP, user-agent, timestamps) seen on your side for org ID aurel-ct-9
> - Any offered indicators of compromise: unusual worker IDs, model variant fallbacks, or cross-customer routing artifacts
> - Recommended containment steps and the Redwood IRP contact for postmortem

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: telemetry_extract_aurelius_20260807.tar.gz (45MB)]

From: Tom Geller <tgeller@aurelius-labs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jessica Park <jessica@aurelius-labs.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual API traffic observed — forensic handoff & SIG/CAIQ evidence request

Marissa / Mateo — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the artifacts. We reviewed the telemetry package with our internal ops; next steps:

- We accept the telemetry snapshot as-is for our internal IR and will provide our full sample request payloads by EOD Monday (UTC).
- Please include the SIG control IDs you referenced in the crosswalk; we need them for our legal/compliance review before we produce a public notification.
- We want a brief postmortem deliverable (one-page timeline + root cause hypothesis + mitigation) once your internal postmortem completes — can you target 6 business days?

We can take the 16:00 UTC bridge if you confirm the calendar invite; Jessica will circulate a short list of prioritized questions ahead of the call.

Tom Geller
Head of Platform Security, Aurelius Labs
[Sent on behalf of Aurelius Security]
